- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5%.
- Underestimate late-period price peaks; adjust forecast upward by 3–8% for the final 5–10 days of the horizon.
- Model tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days; shift forecast forward by 1–2 days for short-term (1–7 day) horizons.
- After a sharp price spike, model overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above the immediate prior peak.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; add a 5–10% downward bias to forecasts if the 30-day average is above 85% of the 90-day moving average.
- For low-price regimes (e.g., <75), model underestimates; increase forecast by 3–7% to avoid missing downward momentum.
- Avoid overfitting to recent volatility; if last 5 days show high variance, reduce forecast sensitivity to those days by 20–30%.
